A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TFLA and mLSTM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DCLM language-modeling results, measured GPU runtime and memory benchmarks, and gate-initialization and normalization experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds full-model training-step timings in Table 6.

M1.justification: The two-level TFLA tiling procedure, forward/backward computations, Algorithm 1 and sigmoid-gated mLSTM variant are unchanged. Condensing the formulations does not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain DCLM next-token prediction at context lengths 4096 and 8192 and the same kernel test scenarios. The added training-time metric concerns existing model/task coverage.

E2.justification: The Llama2-style Transformer reference and FlashAttention, GLA/Simple GLA, Mamba/Mamba 2 and LightningAttention2 comparisons are retained. The new training-time table uses the existing language-modeling comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds full-model training-step time as an evaluation metric for 1.4B models at context length 8192, supplementing the existing kernel timing protocol. The previously reported training budgets, quality evaluation and kernel-benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The numerical-validation checks, fixed-versus-trainable input gates, initialization and epsilon sweeps, transfer-behavior experiments, and memory/head-dimension analyses are retained. Table 6 adds benchmark timings rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify median kernel runtime over 30 iterations after 10 warmup iterations. v3 introduces no additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure; its new timing table contains point values.

E6.justification: v3 Table 6 newly reports training-step times. For 1.4B models with 16 heads, these are 2.39 seconds for Llama and 1.60/1.61/1.62 seconds for EXP LIMIT/EXP XL/SIG XL. v2 lacks these measurements; retained perplexities and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The stabilization and gradient derivations, adaptation to DeltaNet, FLOP/memory formulas and optimal-chunk-size analysis are retained. Equations are consolidated, moved inline or renumbered without substantive changes to the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim two-level sequence parallelism, faster sigmoid-gated mLSTM kernels without language-modeling losses up to 1.4B parameters, and improved stability through gate initialization. Revised conclusion wording does not materially strengthen these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v3 removes the Impact Statement, including its qualification that efficiency savings could be offset by training larger models for longer. The normalization/gating interpretation and limitations concerning numerical instability and theoretical runtime approximations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly specifies sharding a global batch of 256 across 32 GPUs, giving local batch size 8; this does not establish a change to earlier runs. Section 2.1 also omits the explicit affine Q/K/V projection formula. Software versions, training recipe and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Xiong et al. (2020) and Zhu et al. (2025) on normalization, plus Beck et al. (2025), xLSTM 7B, as a larger-model application. The expanded main related-work section largely relocates v2 Appendix A.1 and preserves the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is shortened, GPU fundamentals move to Appendix C.1, and the FlashAttention/FLA discussion moves into Section 6. Equations are condensed and the Impact Statement is removed, while most technical prose remains intact. New perplexity references incorrectly point to Table 6 instead of Table 5.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and repositioning of figures, tables and equations. v3 adds the conceptual comparison diagram in Figure 7 and training-time Table 6; existing plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: Table 6 adds useful full-model timing evidence beyond v2's kernel benchmarks, and Figure 7 helps explain the relationship to prior kernel designs. These limited gains outweigh the removed sustainability qualification and minor editorial regressions, including incorrect perplexity-table references and Figure 7's mislabeled middle panel in its caption. The underlying method and existing empirical evidence remain unchanged.
